chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from whoever mentioned it:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked: 'Is it permissible to say that God is a thing?' He said: 'Yes — it takes Him out of the two limits: the limit of negation (ta'til) and the limit of comparison (tashbih).'

key_terms.حَدّ التَّشْبِيه: Tashbih — the heresy of likening God to creation, anthropomorphism
key_terms.حَدّ التَّعْطِيل: Ta'til — the heresy of denying God any attributes or existence, rendering His nature vacuous
key_terms.شَيْء: Thing — an ontological category affirming existence without specifying modality

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to say that God is a 'thing'?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) was asked whether it is theologically permissible to describe God as 'a thing' (شيء). He affirmed this, explaining that the term preserves divine transcendence by positioning God between two heretical extremes: ta'til (absolute negation of all attributes, associated with theological nihilism) and tashbih (anthropomorphism, comparing God to created things). This middle path is characteristic of the Shia theological tradition of affirming God's existence while negating any similarity to creation.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from the one who mentioned it, said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked, ‘Is it allowed for it to be said that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is a thing?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, taking Him<sup>azwj</sup> out from two limitations – the limitation of the temporariness and the limitation of the resemblance’.
en.sarwar: 7. It is narrated from Imam abu Ja‘far (a.s.)

who said when he was asked, “Is it permissible to say Allah is a thing?” “Yes, it is permissible because it excludes Him from being ignored altogether and from being analogized or considered similar to the creatures.”
